intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene on chromosome X.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is an X-linked, CHARGE-like disorder. Its features are cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977; Pauws et al., 2013). It is caused by splicing mutation in TBX22, the gene that also causes X-linked cleft palate with or without ankyloglossia (CPX) (Pauws et al., 2013).

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) noted that the family they first described (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977) had been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome. On follow-up, they concluded that the affected members of the family did not have CHARGE syndrome or association. Pauws et al. (2013) called the disorder X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.

Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) later described the disorder as X-linked. Pauws et al. (2013) found a TBX22 mutation that tracked with the phenotype in this X-linked family.

paragraphs.text: Pauws et al. (2013) studied the family with X-linked Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome originally reported by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977). In this family they identified a novel splice acceptor mutation in the TBX22 gene (c.593-5T-A) that tracked with the phenotype. In patients with classic CPX, they also identified 2 variants affecting the same exon: a novel splice donor variant (c.767+5G-A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G-A). In silico analysis predicted that all 3 variants would abolish normal mRNA splicing. An in vitro splicing assay indicated that the use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome. Pauws et al. (2013) concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, which expands the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.
